::::: bms-reading-column
Backgammon Made Simple is an open-source project for understanding the game and making better decisions.  The idea is simple:

> **Come with a question. Leave with a clear mental model you can use at the board.**

We try to make difficult ideas clearer, build useful tools, and help more people get excited about backgammon.

## Why We Built This

I started this project while trying to understand my own blunders. The engine gave me the best moves. A friend who is a great player said, “Eventually, you’ll start to see it.”

I wanted to know what I was supposed to see, as I asked questions like:

::: bms-question-examples
[\>]{.bms-code-prefix aria-hidden="true"} *Why is 25% often called the take point... and yet it rarely ever is?*

[\>]{.bms-code-prefix aria-hidden="true"} *When should I run a lone back checker, move it up, or leave it where it is?*

[\>]{.bms-code-prefix aria-hidden="true"} *Why is breaking an anchor brilliant one game and a blunder the next?*

[\>]{.bms-code-prefix aria-hidden="true"} *What can one position teach me about the thousands I'll see later?*

[// goal: clarity over perfection]{.bms-code-note}
:::

Backgammon Made Simple is my attempt to answer questions with real positions, clear explanations, and evidence instead of folklore.

::: bms-section-heading
## Introducing Marty Gale

[ROLE: AUTHOR :: RESEARCHER :: PLAYER]{.bms-heading-meta}
:::

Hi, I'm **Marty Gale, PhD**.[^1]

I research the intersection of dice rigging, probability, and questionable doubling decisions.

Behind the joke, Marty Gale is the public author identity for this project.

I am not presenting myself as one of the world's great backgammon players. I am a curious player learning in public: asking questions, testing ideas, making mistakes, and trying to leave behind explanations that are more useful than a table of rollout results.

## Open Source Tools for the Game

Backgammon Made Simple is also a home for useful technology around the game.

That includes position tools, match-prediction models, reproducible engine comparisons, board-rendering software, public datasets, and research code. Where it is practical and responsible, the methods and tools will be made public so other people can inspect them, reuse them, and build something better.

The website is the main product. The software exists to support clearer learning, stronger evidence, more interesting questions, and greater interest in the game.

## Built to Be Useful

The project does not need to explain the whole game before it becomes useful.

It can begin with one good question, one position, and one explanation that changes how someone sees the board.

That is the standard I am trying to meet.
